critical_caveats: S_inference is an Amdahl UPPER BOUND assuming per-component cost gamma=2-4x Gaussian and ZERO overhead (tree traversal/gating/normalization/compositing/adaptive maintenance unmeasured). NOT a real GPU speedup.

G2 benefit-budget adds a break-even overhead h_max: a future renderer must keep real overhead <= ~26.6% (gamma=2) / ~20.7% (gamma=4) for the 3x target to survive. Necessary condition, not evidence 3x is achievable.
Fitting is per-view (teacher = that view's rasterization); measures low-rank compressibility of the local transfer response, NOT cross-view 3D-consistent representation (that is G5 native training).
Held-out is held-out PIXELS within a view, not held-out VIEWS; plan sec.9 G1 'test new views / occlusion change' only partially addressed (no cross-view generalization certificate).

G2 rigorous interval-arithmetic certificate (validated) PROVES the student does NOT reproduce the teacher everywhere on the continuous tile domain (pass_rate 0.62-0.75 < 1.0). This is a per-tile fixed-view bound, NOT a camera/view-variation bound and NOT a GPU throughput bound.
Component-count reduction is not a GPU speedup; real speedup requires G3/G4 (and a fused spatial-tree kernel, not implemented).
fail_closed: Did not relax gates post-hoc, did not delete hard tiles, did not report unweighted Gaussian counts as speedup, did not convert Amdahl bound into a speedup claim. Higher rank worsens Jacobian (non-monotonic); did not auto-upgrade rank.

G1_sub_analysis_failure_localization.note: Incompressible work is a diffuse ~9-19% tile-count tail (0.6% by work), not concentrated in deep deciles; top-N pruning insufficient. Reclassified as a G1 occlusion-change sub-analysis (plan sec.9 G1), not the G2 gate.

binding_overhead_budget.note: G3 measured overhead must be <= ~26.6% (gamma=2) / ~20.7% (gamma=4) for 3x to survive. Zero-overhead bound only; NOT a speedup claim.

G2_benefit_budget.note: G2 = sec.9 benefit-budget stop-rule. Uses measured G1 p*f=q_weighted; r=gamma; solves break-even overhead h. No fabricated GPU cost.

G3_gpu_microbenchmark.finding: 4 scenes (bicycle, room r5k/r30k, garden). Intrinsic launch-free math gamma median R4=26.4x (range ~1.3-78x, scene-dependent via M_rep/R), but per-tile launch-bound gamma collapses to ~1.65-1.82x; measured per-tile S with dispatch overhead ~1.38-1.49x, far below 3x. Non-monotonic in rank.
G3_gpu_microbenchmark.not_a_speedup_claim: LOCAL per-tile kernel ratio, NOT end-to-end renderer speedup.

G4_gpu_microbenchmark.finding: Student per-tile latency drops 181x from B=1 to B=256; batching recovers the 6-14x math headroom. Per-tile 1.2x is a launch-granularity artifact. TRUE G4 microbenchmark (fused CUDA kernel vs gsplat) still NOT_REACHED.

G2_continuous_domain_certificate.method_dense: Deterministic dense sub-pixel grid (sub=4, 4096 pts/tile) per tile; 3 scenes x 10 tiles x 3 ranks = 90 tiles/rank.
G2_continuous_domain_certificate.method_rigorous: Branch-and-bound interval arithmetic over tile 2D ray domain; student interval box = convex hull of rank-R expert predictions; validated on synthetic (bound/pointmax ~1.0-4.6).
G2_continuous_domain_certificate.finding: DENSE (empirical) pooled pass_rate 0.98/0.90/0.90 (rank 4/8/16); worst-tile max|E,T| up to 0.78. RIGOROUS (interval-arithmetic, validated) pooled pass_rate 0.75/0.63/0.62; the bound PROVES the student does NOT reproduce the teacher everywhere on the continuous domain (fails 0.02 gate on a non-empty tile set). Higher rank does NOT monotonically improve either metric. This TEMPERS any 'student reproduces teacher everywhere' claim with a proof, not a sample.
G2_continuous_domain_certificate.not_a_speedup_claim: Fidelity certificate only; says nothing about GPU throughput.
